AuditFinding.observationDetails:
Review of the user access management controls over the in-scope systems revealed the following:

1. Inadequate Segregation of Duties (SoD) over AWS IAM and Backup Administration. In the AWS environment, the System Administrator account "april.claudio", managed by a DevOps Officer under Cloud Infrastructure, who is responsible for IAM configuration and user access provisioning is also responsible for managing backups for DynamoDB and RDS. The same account has broad resource privileges allowing it to initiate, modify, and restore backups across the in- scope AWS resources. This combination creates a “single point of compromise” where a single actor (or a compromised credential) can execute an end-to-end attack and reduce your ability to detect or recover. 

2. Roles with excessive access. Our review of the role-based access matrix of the in- scope systems noted three (3) roles that are privileged having excessive operational functions, and eight (8) regular user roles with combined maker and approver functions. Refer to Annex B for further details. 

3. Current User Access Review practice does not cover user appropriateness. The Cybersecurity team is conducting a user access review focused on validating the status of active and inactive user accounts across systems. However, this review does not include an assessment of the appropriateness of user roles defined in the manually maintained user access matrix which could identify potential updates or changes to access rights and permissions. As a result, SoD issues noted in the previous item were not detected. 

Currently, the evaluation of role appropriateness and validity is performed for: 
• Onboarding: Prior to granting access for new joiners. 
• Offboarding: Access revocation for employees who have resigned or left the organization

This means this was not covered by the periodic review being performed to ensure that existing user roles remain aligned with job responsibilities and organizational changes.
AuditFinding.risks:
- Concentration of access provisioning, privilege management, and backup administration within a single identity introduces confidentiality, integrity, and availability risks.


- Roles with combined maker-approver functions eliminate independent validation and increase the likelihood of unauthorized, fraudulent, or erroneous transactions.


If the DevOps officer (or anyone who gets control of that account) is malicious or compromised, they can:

1. Create or elevate access without oversight. Create new IAM users/roles, attach admin policies, modify permission boundaries, update trust policies, or provision access to production resources.


2. Access or change production data. Use the elevated permissions to query/modify RDS data, export DynamoDB tables, or access related S3/KMS resources.


3. Use backup/restore powers to bypass controls or hide activity. 

 a)Restore an RDS snapshot / DynamoDB backup into a less-controlled environment (another VPC/account, weaker monitoring) to read data outside normal access paths.


 b)Copy/export snapshots/backups (where allowed) to another account/region for exfiltration.


 c)Modify retention/backup plans to shorten retention or exclude specific resources.


 D)Delete backups/snapshots (or disable Point-in-Time Recovery / PITR) to reduce recoverability. This is especially damaging in ransomware/destructive scenarios.


4. SoD conflicts and excessive privileges may remain undetected due to the absence of structured review of role appropriateness.
AuditFinding.recommendation:
1. Split IAM administration and backup/database administration to different personnel or roles.
 
2. Re-design system roles to align with segregation of duties principles by separating initiation, approval, and administrative functions. 

3. Update the access matrix to incorporate explicit SoD requirements and evaluate potential conflicts arising from business processes across systems. 

4. Expand the periodic user access review to include validation of role appropriateness, least privilege alignment, and SoD conflicts
AuditFinding.managementResponse:
1 – The DevOps function inherently requires elevated and privileged access to critical infrastructure and cloud environments. We acknowledge that such access, if not properly governed, may represent a potential single point of compromise. To mitigate this risk, the management implemented the following compensating controls: 

a. Quarterly User Access Reviews (UAR): All privileged and elevated access rights undergo formal quarterly review to validate appropriateness, enforce least privilege, and remove any unnecessary or excessive permissions. 

b. Continuous Threat Detection & Response Monitoring: Their cloud environment is monitored by a threat detection and response solution that identifies malicious, abnormal, or anomalous behavior. 

This monitoring applies to all users, including members of the DevOps team, ensuring that privileged activity remains visible, auditable, and subject to investigation when required. T

his observation is acknowledged. The team had already identified this as a gap in the existing scope of our User Access Review (UAR) process, even prior to the current audit exercise. As a corrective measure moving forward, they are conducting an enterprise-wide access re-baseline across all systems and departments. 

The objective is to establish a definitive view of current access entitlements, ensure all permissions are properly documented and justified, and strengthen oversight over privilege assignments. This re-baseline will also enable them to detect access creep or gradual elevation of privileges early, allowing them to remediate excessive or inappropriate access at the earliest possible stage.

AuditFinding.auditObservation: Untimely deactivation of user access to in-scope systems
AuditFinding.observationDetails: The User Access Management Policy requires immediate revocation of user access upon termination. However, review of 14 separated user accounts showed that 4 (29%) were deactivated after their separation dates, indicating delays in access removal beyond the employees’ last working day. Despite these delays, audit and activity log review did not identify any evidence of unauthorized access or activity occurring after the users’ separation dates.
AuditFinding.risks: Although no unauthorized activities were detected, the delay in revoking access indicates a control gap that could potentially compromise system security and operational integrity.
AuditFinding.recommendation:
1. Consistently implement formal offboarding workflow requiring HR to notify the Tech Team immediately upon employee termination. Tech Team must deactivate user accounts on the employee’s last working day, and confirmation of deactivation should be documented.

2. Consider automating alerts for deactivation to flag any accounts that remain active beyond the termination date, ensuring timely remediation.
AuditFinding.managementResponse: The observation is acknowledged. The CSeC team is already aware of this finding. As a proactive measure, the team is currently implementing Single Sign-On (SSO) across compatible applications. This initiative is expected to improve adherence to timely user deactivation requirements.

"Initial Response during the Washup Meeting last Feb 04, 2026: The technology team has acknowledged the observation and will consider the recommendations.

This is observation is acknowledged. The Csec team is well-aware of this finding/observation. As our proactive measure, the team is currently working on implementing SSO to our compatible apps. This initiative should be able to increase our adherence to timely deactivation."

AuditFinding.auditObservation: Inadequate password parameter requirements in Access Management Policy
AuditFinding.observationDetails:
The PDAX Access Management Policy lacked several key controls necessary for secure user authentication. Specifically, the policy did not define password requirements for:
a. Use of a one-time password for initial logon
b. Maximum number of unsuccessful logon attempts before account lockout
c. User capabilities to reset accounts after lockout
d. User capabilities to assign their own passwords
e. Password history restrictions
f. Idle session timeout configurations
g. Duration before idle session timeout
h. Logging of unsuccessful logon attempts

As a result, password controls were inconsistently implemented across in-scope systems, and the policy was not fully aligned with industry best practices for secure authentication. See Annex E for further details.

**Note on Compensating Control**
While the system’s user access was not integrated with Active Directory, a compensating MFA control has been implemented. Users were required to provide a one-time password (OTP) sent via text message or email for authentication, adding an additional layer of security.
AuditFinding.risks:
- The absence of defined password controls increases the risk of unauthorized access, account compromise, and potential security breaches.

- Inconsistent application of password policies may weaken system security and expose sensitive data.
AuditFinding.recommendation:
1. Update the Access Management Policy to include detailed password controls covering initial logon, complexity, change frequency, lockout thresholds, account reset procedures, user-assigned passwords, password history, idle session timeouts, and logging of unsuccessful attempts.

2. Systems should be configured consistently to enforce these requirements, and periodic reviews should be conducted to ensure compliance across all in-scope systems.
AuditFinding.managementResponse: This observation is acknowledged. As an additional note, our strategic direction is to gradually move away from traditional Active Directory–centric identity management. We are transitioning toward broader implementation of centralized Single Sign-On (SSO) across enterprise applications, as well as extending identity federation to workplace device access (e.g., laptops). This will support stronger access governance, improved visibility, and a more modern, scalable identity architecture.

AuditFinding.auditObservation: No Formal Policy Established for Audit Logging and Monitoring
AuditFinding.observationDetails:
While in-scope systems can generate and retain an audit trail, PDX did not have a formally established and approved Audit Logging and Monitoring Policy that would define the current process on types of events to log, retention periods, monitoring frequency, review procedures, and escalation protocols.

While this was the case, our review confirmed that logging was enabled and captured key events, including:
a. Access activity (e.g., successful and unsuccessful login attempts)
b. Transaction details (event type, initiator, and timestamp)
c. Event severity assessments from system monitoring

In addition, the Cybersecurity Team conducted regular monitoring of system logs and followed a standard practice to address any activities identified. The Team also confirmed that user access logs were reviewed quarterly in accordance with the PDAX Access Management Policy.

Due to the absence of formal policy requirements for audit logging and monitoring procedures, response activities for security alerts were not consistently documented in incident reports and were only communicated via email. As a result, details of the alerts, investigation steps, and resolution activities were not formally captured, limiting traceability and auditability of security events.
AuditFinding.risks: Without a formally approved logging and monitoring policy, there is a risk that critical events may not be consistently monitored or reviewed, potentially allowing security incidents or operational anomalies to go undetected.
AuditFinding.recommendation:
1. Establish and formally approve an Audit Logging and Monitoring Policy that defines the types of events to log, retention periods, monitoring frequency, review procedures, and escalation protocols.

2. Audit logs should be periodically reviewed and documented to ensure consistent monitoring, traceability, and alignment with regulatory requirements.
AuditFinding.managementResponse: This observation is acknowledged. To fully address the identified gap, the Company will develop and implement a stand-alone Audit Logging and Monitoring Policy. This policy will explicitly define the required event types, data retention periods, review frequencies, and escalation protocols needed to ensure consistent and effective monitoring.
AuditFinding.remarks: This observation is acknowledged. To fully address this gap, the Company will draft and implement a standalone Audit Logging and Monitoring Policy that explicitly defines the required event types, data retention periods, review frequencies, and escalation protocols.

AuditFinding.auditObservation: Lapses in Third-Party User Access Management Process
AuditFinding.observationDetails:
1. Lack of formalized procedure for reviewing the access granted to vendors, consultants, and other external users. 

The existing policy and procedure does not specifically provide guidance that will govern the provisioning and reviewing of access granted to external parties.
- Lack of documented criteria for evaluating access requests from vendors and consultants; and
- No defined workflow or roles and responsibilities for requesting, reviewing and approving such access.

Additionally, upon inspection of access provisioning documents, IAD noted that there is no proper documentation to support that Cybersecurity Team assessed the access request for any potential threat to the security of PDAX systems prior to actual access granting. There is also no proper documentation in place to support that Cybersecurity Team validated if the actual access implemented in the system is appropriate based on the approved user access request.

2. Lapses in the third-party user access creation and modification process.

I. Lack of cybersecurity oversight in the third-party vendor access provisioning. TCH-SIS-P001 Access Management Policy requires that Cybersecurity Team to be copied in all access-related requests or modifications to all local files, cloud-based files, application components, features and functional modules.

However, IAD noted that in two (2) out of five (5) sampled third-party users, the Cybersecurity team was not included in the email communications related to the provisioning of access to these users. Refer to Table 2 for the details.

II. Eight (8) out of ten (10) third-party users selected for testing that have access to Figma (a tool used for website design) were not supported by properly documented user access requests and approval from the Division/Department Head. Refer to Table 3  for the details.

III. Provisioning of third-party user access prior to formal review and approval. Per inspection of the ticket requests related to sample third-party users, IAD noted that system access for certain third-party users was provisioned prior to the formal request and approval. Refer to Table 4 for the details.

3. Insufficient third-party user access monitoring control.

Cybersecurity Department conducts enterprise-wide user access review, encompassing access of third-party users in PDAX systems, tools and applications on a quarterly basis. However, IAD noted the procedure does not fully capture any movements, such as creation or termination of access for vendors, consultants, and other external users, that occur between quarters.

The Cybersecurity Department maintains a list of all of the users with access to all of the systems, tools and applications in PDAX. However, IAD noted instances of third-party users tagged as deactivated in the monitoring file but active in Google Workspace. Per further inspection, this user has been deactivated but reactivated upon the request of the Department Head. Refer to Table 6 for the details.
AuditFinding.rootCause: Absence of formally established procedures and monitoring controls that specifically governs the end-to-end management of third-party access (creation, modification, and termination).
AuditFinding.risks: Risk of inappropriate access resulting from lapses in the processing of third-party user access creation, modification and review. Without proper authorization, timely updates, and consistent monitoring, third-party users may retain excessive or outdated access privileges, potentially leading to unauthorized data exposure, misuse of system resources, or security breaches.
AuditFinding.impact:
Operational Impact/Information Security

Weak access control governance allows departments to bypass the Cybersecurity team, fostering unauthorized system use and increasing the risk of data leakage, intellectual property loss, and compliance violations. The absence of accurate monitoring and documentation also reduces audit readiness and creates operational inefficiencies.
AuditFinding.recommendation:
Update policies and procedures to:
● Clearly define roles and responsibilities for requesting, approving, provisioning, modifying and terminating third-party user access;
● Require documented approval prior to granting access and upon any changes to access rights; and
● Implement monitoring controls to timely detect potential security threats in PDAX systems.
AuditFinding.managementResponse: RMD acknowledged the observation and noted that this is under the purview of the Cybersecurity Department under the Quarterly UAR exercise. RMD will coordinate and discuss with the Cybersecurity Department regarding the actual application of the User Access Management Process for Third-Party users.

InformationAsset.businessImpact:
• Unauthorized disclosure of the Contract of Application could expose vendor pricing, security commitments, and commercial terms stored in Google Drive, undermining PDAX negotiating leverage and revealing security architecture details to adversaries.
• If the Contract of Application owned by the department is exfiltrated, attackers gain detailed knowledge of PDAX's application security requirements and vendor dependencies, enabling targeted attacks on customer crypto wallets, custody systems, and trading infrastructure that could result in loss of customer funds and BSP regulatory action
• Tampering or loss of these contracts could create compliance gaps with BSP vendor risk management expectations and weaken the cybersecurity department's ability to enforce vendor security obligations.
InformationAsset.threat:
• Insiders or compromised DevSecOps member accounts with Google Drive access could exfiltrate the Contract of Application, exposing sensitive vendor agreements and security commitments.
• DevSecOps members with legitimate access to the Contract of Application in Google Drive could become insider threats, stealing sensitive contract terms to benefit competitors or manipulating clauses to bypass security controls for personal crypto trading advantages
• Phishing or Business Email Compromise targeting DevSecOps members such as Julius Faa or Patrick Galinato could lead to credential theft and unauthorized access to Google Drive where the contracts are stored.
InformationAsset.vulnerability:
• A01 Broken Access Control - Google Drive sharing permissions for the Contract of Application may extend beyond the named DevSecOps owners, allowing unauthorized users to view or download sensitive vendor contracts (A01:2025 Broken Access Control; No public CVE)
• A01 Broken Access Control: The Contract of Application owned by the department stored in Google Drive suffers from overly broad sharing permissions that grant unnecessary access to PDAX employees beyond the DevSecOps team, violating least privilege and enabling unauthorized disclosure of sensitive vendor terms (A01:2025 Broken Access Control; No public CVE)
• A09 Security Logging and Alerting Failures - Access and download activity for the Contract of Application in Google Drive may not be fully monitored or alerted on, creating blind spots for unauthorized exfiltration consistent with ORCA risk CYB-2-3 (A07:2025 Authentication Failures; No public CVE)

• Compromise of Slack Information could expose internal communications about wallet infrastructure, trading systems, and KYC/AML procedures, enabling targeted attacks on PDAX customer crypto and fiat assets.
• Customer fiat and crypto assets are jeopardized if Slack abuse reveals wallet private keys or trading system credentials, enabling theft and violating BSP custody rules.
• Disruption or unauthorized access to Slack Information could leak employee credentials and security workflows, triggering BSP regulatory findings and Data Privacy Act breach notification obligations.
InformationAsset.threat:
• Malware on employee endpoints could steal Slack session tokens or OAuth credentials, mirroring the Nikkei breach where malware-enabled credential theft exposed sensitive data from over 17,000 users.
• External attackers launch phishing or endpoint malware campaigns to steal Slack credentials, then pivot to PDAX production systems and exfiltrate customer identity and wallet data.
• Phishing or spear-phishing attacks targeting PDAX employees could compromise Slack accounts, allowing attackers to exfiltrate sensitive channel data and impersonate staff for social engineering against crypto customers.
InformationAsset.vulnerability:
• Slack OAuth tokens and session credentials stored on endpoints may be stolen by malware or phishing, enabling unauthorized workspace access without triggering additional authentication challenges (A07:2025 Authentication Failures; CVE-2026-44695)
• A02 Security Misconfiguration: Slack access tokens can be exposed through vulnerable third-party integrations such as WP SlackSync ( .5 High), enabling unauthorized access to PDAX channels containing sensitive KYC/AML discussions and wallet infrastructure details (A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration; CVE-2019-14366)
• Overly permissive Slack workspace configurations, such as public channels containing sensitive operational details or excessive third-party integration scopes, could expose internal PDAX data to unauthorized users (A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration; CVE-2024-54682)

• If NordPass User Management is disrupted, PDAX cybersecurity staff cannot provision or revoke password vault access during onboarding and offboarding, leaving departing employees with active credentials to critical systems such as Jumpcloud, Google Workspace, and Slack
• NordPass User Management disruption prevents admins from adding or removing employee access to production systems, halting trading, wallet custody, and KYC/AML processing and violating BSP operational continuity requirements.
• If NordPass User Management is abused, an attacker who adds a rogue user or deletes legitimate admins gains access to stored credentials for production wallet infrastructure, trading systems, and fiat rail accounts, risking unauthorized crypto transfers and BSP and AML compliance violations
InformationAsset.threat:
• Phishing or business email compromise targeting NordPass admins Julius Faa or Jayson Erasga could result in account takeover, allowing attackers to add unauthorized users and harvest credentials for every PDAX system stored in the vault
• Phishing and Business Email Compromise attacks targeting NordPass admins can compromise credentials, allowing attackers to perform unauthorized user additions and deletions that grant access to PDAX production systems.
• Malware on an admin endpoint could exploit the NordPass browser extension clickjacking zero-day disclosed at DEF CON 33 to auto-fill stored corporate credentials into malicious pages, enabling lateral movement to wallet and custody infrastructure
InformationAsset.vulnerability:
• NordPass browser extension was affected by a zero-day clickjacking vulnerability disclosed at DEF CON 33 in August 2025 that allowed malicious websites to trick the extension into auto-filling credentials, enabling credential theft from admins managing PDAX user accounts; maps to A01 Broken Access Control (A01:2025 Broken Access Control; No public CVE)
• NordPass browser extension contains zero-day clickjacking vulnerabilities that could trick admins into performing unintended user management actions without explicit consent (A06:2025 Insecure Design; No public CVE)
• NordPass admin accounts for Julius Faa and Jayson Erasga may be vulnerable to phishing or credential stuffing with no confirmed MFA enforcement on the admin panel, allowing unauthorized addition or deletion of vault users; maps to A07 Authentication Failures (A04:2025 Cryptographic Failures; No public CVE)

• NordPass autofill on non-exact URL matches could inject credentials into lookalike domains, enabling credential theft through typosquatting (A06:2025 Insecure Design; No public CVE)

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Delayed pentest engagement may result in prolonged exposure to unidentified and unremediated security vulnerabilities.
OrcaRisk.cause: Lack of manpower. Numerous internal applications that needs to be tested.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: 1. VAPT Roadmap
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: The VAPT Roadmap provides a structured schedule for identifying, prioritizing, and planning applications for security testing. However, the control Needs Improvement because a roadmap alone may not ensure timely execution when testing resources are insufficient. Improvements are required in risk-based prioritization, resource and capacity planning, defined testing frequencies, monitoring of delayed engagements, escalation of overdue assessments, and management of approved testing exceptions.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Unidentified vulnerabilities may remain exposed, increasing the risk of exploitation, data breach, regulatory findings, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Moderate because limited testing resources and the large number of internal applications may repeatedly delay planned penetration-testing engagements. This may allow unidentified vulnerabilities to remain exposed for extended periods, increasing the risk of exploitation, data exposure, regulatory findings, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: The VAPT Roadmap improves visibility and prioritization of planned assessments; however, the residual risk remains Possible and Moderate because limited manpower may continue to delay testing activities. Applications awaiting assessment may still contain unidentified vulnerabilities that could be exploited before the scheduled penetration test is completed.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Incomplete VAPT coverage may result in unidentified security vulnerabilities across critical systems, applications, or infrastructure, increasing the likelihood of undetected exploitation, control gaps, and audit or regulatory findings.
OrcaRisk.cause: Non inclusion in scope due to engagement limitation
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
1. Scoping call document
2. VAPT Policy and Internal VAPT Playbook
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: The scoping-call document, VAPT Policy, and Internal VAPT Playbook establish requirements for defining, documenting, and approving the assessment scope. However, the controls Need Improvement because systems may still be excluded due to time, budget, access, technical, or engagement constraints. Improvements are required in maintaining a complete asset-to-VAPT coverage inventory, formally documenting exclusions, conducting risk assessments for out-of-scope assets, obtaining management approval, establishing compensating controls, and scheduling excluded systems for subsequent testing.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Security gaps in critical systems may remain undetected, resulting in possible exploitation, audit findings, and BSP compliance issues.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Possible and Major because engagement limitations may result in critical systems, applications, infrastructure components, or interfaces being excluded from the agreed VAPT scope. Undetected security weaknesses may consequently remain within the environment, potentially resulting in exploitation, control gaps, audit findings, and BSP compliance issues.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: The documented scoping process and VAPT governance requirements improve accountability over assessment coverage. However, the residual risk remains Possible and Moderate because approved or unintentional scope exclusions may still leave critical assets untested, allowing material vulnerabilities to remain undetected until a future assessment or security incident occurs.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Failure to remediate vulnerabilities may leave known vulnerabilities exploitable, increasing the risk of unauthorized access, data exposure, service disruption, regulatory findings, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.cause: Non commitment of engineering teams in remediation sprints
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
Internal VAPT Playbook
SLAs for PenTest findings remediation
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: The Internal VAPT Playbook and remediation SLAs provide a defined approach for managing penetration-testing findings. However, control effectiveness requires stronger enforcement of remediation timelines, escalation of overdue findings, validation of closure, and monitoring of SLA compliance.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Known vulnerabilities may be exploited, leading to unauthorized access, data exposure, service disruption, and regulatory non-compliance.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Major because insufficient commitment from engineering teams may repeatedly delay or prevent remediation of known vulnerabilities, potentially resulting in unauthorized access, data exposure, service disruption, and regulatory non-compliance.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: The Internal VAPT Playbook and remediation SLAs reduce the likelihood and impact to Possible and Moderate; however, overdue findings may remain exploitable due to weak SLA enforcement, limited escalation, or inadequate closure validation.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Delayed remediation of identified vulnerabilities may prolong exposure to known security weaknesses, increasing the likelihood of exploitation, data compromise, service disruption, regulatory findings, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.cause: Due to lack of resources (Manpower)
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: Established a vulnerability management tracker that monitors who's the assigned squad to remediate the vulnerability
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: The vulnerability management tracker improves accountability by identifying the squad responsible for remediation. However, it should be enhanced with risk-based prioritization, defined due dates, escalation procedures, aging analysis, remediation evidence, and independent closure validation.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Prolonged exposure to known weaknesses may increase the likelihood of cyberattack, data compromise, operational disruption, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Likely and Minor because resource and manpower limitations may delay remediation activities, prolonging exposure to known weaknesses even when the immediate impact of individual findings is limited.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: The vulnerability management tracker reduces the likelihood to Rare by assigning remediation ownership. However, exploitation of an overdue vulnerability may still have a Moderate impact, particularly where prioritization, escalation, and closure validation remain insufficient.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Delayed detection of security incidents or data breaches may prolong threat actor activity, increase the scope of compromise, and result in greater data exposure, financial loss, regulatory findings, and reputational damage.

OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Threat actors may remain active longer, increasing the scope of compromise, data exposure, financial loss, and regulatory impact.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because inadequate security-tool configuration may repeatedly prevent timely detection of incidents, allowing threat actors to remain active, expand the compromise, expose data, disrupt operations, and create significant financial and regulatory consequences.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Baseline controls, endpoint security requirements, MSOC notifications, and AWS GuardDuty reduce the risk to Possible and Major. However, configuration gaps, incomplete coverage, false negatives, and delayed alert investigation may still allow significant incidents to remain undetected.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Alert fatigue caused by excessive or low-quality security alerts may result in analysts overlooking critical threats, delaying incident response, and increasing the risk of undetected compromise, data exposure, service disruption, and reputational damage.

OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Critical alerts may be missed, resulting in delayed incident response, undetected compromise, data exposure, and service disruption
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Possible and Major because the high volume of AWS, Provintell, and internal-user alerts may overwhelm analysts, causing critical alerts to be overlooked and delaying response to potentially significant security incidents.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: The intelligence tracker provides visibility and accountability, but the residual risk remains Possible and Moderate because alert quality, prioritization, triage, escalation, and closure monitoring still require improvement.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Incomplete visibility across the IT environment may create security blind spots, limiting the organization’s ability to detect threats, assess exposure, and respond effectively, thereby increasing the risk of undetected compromise, data exposure, service disruption, and regulatory findings.
OrcaRisk.cause:
Incomplete asset inventory - Not all servers, endpoints, cloud resources, applications, APIs, databases, and third-party systems are properly identified and tracked.

Systems not onboarded to monitoring tools - Some assets may not be integrated with SIEM, EDR, CSPM, vulnerability scanners, log management, or alerting platforms.

Lack of centralized logging - Security logs may be stored separately across different platforms, making it difficult to correlate events and detect suspicious activity.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: Minimum Baseline Security Controls, Endpoint Security Policy, MSOC integration in security email distro, AWS Guard Duty Alerts
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Existing baseline, endpoint, MSOC, and AWS monitoring controls provide partial security visibility. However, gaps may remain in system coverage, alert correlation, continuous monitoring, response procedures, and validation that alerts result in timely and appropriate action.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Security blind spots may prevent timely threat detection and response, leading to undetected compromise and regulatory findings.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Major because incomplete asset inventories, monitoring-tool coverage, and centralized logging may regularly create security blind spots, preventing timely detection and response across critical systems and infrastructure.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Existing baseline, endpoint, MSOC, and AWS monitoring controls reduce the likelihood to Unlikely. However, the impact remains Major because an incident involving an unmonitored critical asset could still cause substantial data exposure, disruption, or regulatory findings.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Mishandling or delayed containment of an active threat may allow the threat actor to maintain access, expand the scope of compromise, exfiltrate sensitive data, disrupt critical services, and increase financial, regulatory, and reputational impact.
OrcaRisk.cause:
Lack of documented incident response playbooks - Teams may not have predefined steps for malware, compromised accounts, phishing, data breach, ransomware, insider threat, or cloud compromise scenarios.

Poor coordination between teams - Cybersecurity, IT, DevOps, IAM, Ops, CS, Workplace, Legal, Compliance, Communications, and business teams may not be aligned during incident response.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: Tech Incident Handling Procedure, IR playbooks
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: The Technology Incident Handling Procedure and incident-response playbooks provide a structured response framework. However, effectiveness should be strengthened through regular tabletop exercises, defined response metrics, updated escalation contacts, scenario-specific testing, evidence retention, and lessons-learned tracking.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Threat actors may expand access, exfiltrate data, disrupt services, and increase financial, regulatory, and reputational impact.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because inadequate playbooks and poor cross-functional coordination may repeatedly delay containment of active threats, allowing attackers to expand access, exfiltrate sensitive data, and disrupt critical services.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: The Technology Incident Handling Procedure and incident-response playbooks reduce the risk to Unlikely and Moderate. Residual exposure remains because untested playbooks, outdated escalation contacts, or coordination failures may still delay containment.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Inability to perform accurate post-incident forensics and root cause analysis may prevent the organization from determining the true cause, scope, and impact of a security incident, leading to incomplete remediation, recurring incidents, regulatory findings, and continued exposure to similar threats.
OrcaRisk.cause:
Lack of centralized log management - Logs may be scattered across multiple systems, making it difficult to reconstruct the timeline of events.

Poor log quality or missing event details - Logs may lack key fields such as user ID, source IP, device ID, timestamp, session ID, API activity, affected records, or administrative actions.

Third-party visibility gaps - Vendors, cloud providers, outsourced teams, or managed service providers may not provide sufficient logs, evidence, or investigation support.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: MSOC Investigation/Analysis
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: MSOC investigation and analysis provides detective and investigative capability. However, improvements are required in investigation timelines, documentation standards, escalation criteria, root-cause identification, case tracking, quality assurance, and validation that recommended actions are implemented.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Root cause may remain unresolved, resulting in incomplete remediation, recurring incidents, and continued exposure to similar threats.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Minor because missing, incomplete, or decentralized logs may repeatedly hinder forensic investigation and root-cause analysis, although the direct impact may initially be limited to incomplete remediation and investigation delays.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: MSOC investigation and analysis reduce the likelihood to Possible, while the impact remains Minor. Residual risk persists where log quality, third-party evidence, case documentation, and root-cause validation are insufficient.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Ineffective proactive threat identification may limit the organization’s ability to detect emerging threats, identify attack patterns, and address weaknesses before exploitation, increasing the risk of undetected compromise, data exposure, service disruption, and regulatory or reputational impact.

OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Periodic threat-intelligence activities and dissemination through a dedicated Slack channel improve security awareness. However, the process should be formalized to ensure intelligence is timely, relevant, risk-assessed, assigned for action, tracked to closure, and integrated into monitoring and defensive controls.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Emerging threats may not be detected early, increasing the likelihood of compromise, data breach, and operational disruption.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Moderate because heavy reliance on reactive MSOC and AWS alerts may regularly prevent early identification of emerging threats, increasing the possibility of compromise, data exposure, and operational disruption.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Periodic threat intelligence and dissemination through Slack reduce the risk to Unlikely and Minor. However, emerging threats may still be missed when intelligence is not timely, formally assessed, assigned for action, or integrated into security controls.

OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Existing access management and deactivation controls provide partial mitigation. However, the control should be improved through event-driven access reviews, timely role updates, clear reviewer accountability, validation against current job responsibilities, and monitoring of overdue actions.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Employees may retain access unrelated to their new role, resulting in unauthorized activity, data exposure, and policy violations.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because failure to trigger access reviews following employee transfers may regularly leave obsolete privileges active, potentially enabling unauthorized access to sensitive systems and data.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Existing access-management and deactivation controls reduce the risk to Unlikely and Moderate. Residual exposure remains where role changes are not communicated promptly or previous access is not completely identified and removed.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Review fatigue leading to inaccurate access certifications
OrcaRisk.cause: Lack of manpower and large number of access requests
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: Utilize automation and workflows to ease the burden of huge number of requests.
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: The existing control doesn't really answer the risk here of review fatigue, it may alleviate the risk a little however additional manpower is still needed.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Access reviewers may approve inappropriate access, leading to excessive privileges, unauthorized access, and audit findings.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Moderate because limited manpower and a high number of access requests may repeatedly cause reviewer fatigue, increasing the likelihood of inaccurate certifications, excessive privileges, and audit findings.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Automated access-review workflows reduce the risk to Unlikely and Minor by streamlining certification activities, providing timely notifications, and improving tracking and escalation. However, inaccurate certifications may still occur where reviewers rely excessively on automated recommendations, fail to validate actual business need, or approve access without adequate supporting information.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Retention of administrative privileges by users who no longer need them
OrcaRisk.cause: Lack of access reviews, lack of checking for appropriateness and existence of access
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
User Access Review
Access Deactivation Procedure 
Access Management Procedure
MBSS
Information Security Policy
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Access management policies, procedures, reviews, and baseline security requirements are in place. However, improvements are needed in privileged-access identification, approval, periodic recertification, activity monitoring, emergency-access control, and timely removal of unnecessary privileges.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Users may retain powerful access rights, increasing the risk of privilege misuse, system compromise, and unauthorized changes.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because inadequate access reviews and appropriateness checks may regularly allow users to retain administrative privileges, potentially enabling system compromise, unauthorized changes, and significant data exposure.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Access-management controls reduce the risk to Unlikely and Moderate. However, unnecessary administrative access may remain where privileged accounts are not separately inventoried, monitored, recertified, and promptly removed.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Unmonitored physical intrusion via tailgating
OrcaRisk.cause: Irregular review of physical access logs and CCTV, combined with a lack of anti-tailgating physical controls
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: Physical Access Review
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Physical access reviews provide a mechanism for identifying inappropriate access to restricted areas. However, the control should be strengthened through defined review frequency, reconciliation with active personnel records, timely badge deactivation, visitor monitoring, exception management, and evidence retention.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Unauthorized individuals may access restricted areas, resulting in theft, tampering, data exposure, and physical security breaches
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Moderate because irregular review of physical-access logs and CCTV, together with limited anti-tailgating measures, may repeatedly allow unauthorized individuals to enter restricted areas.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Physical access reviews reduce the risk to Rare and Minor. Limited residual exposure remains from tailgating, missed CCTV events, delayed badge deactivation, or ineffective visitor supervision.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Former employees retaining access to sensitive corporate data or VPNs post-termination
OrcaRisk.cause: Delayed notification to access management personnel. Delayed deactivation of access.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
User Access Review
Access Deactivation Procedure 
Access Management Procedure
MBSS
Information Security Policy
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Access deactivation and review controls are established. However, stronger integration with employee offboarding, defined deactivation timelines, escalation of delayed removals, validation across all systems, and monitoring of exceptions are required to ensure access is removed promptly.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Ex-employees may access corporate systems or data, resulting in data leakage, sabotage, fraud, and regulatory findings.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because delayed offboarding notifications and access deactivation may regularly allow former employees to retain access to corporate systems, sensitive data, or VPN services, potentially resulting in fraud, sabotage, or data leakage.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Access-deactivation and review controls reduce the risk to Unlikely and Minor. Residual exposure remains where offboarding notices are delayed, some applications are excluded, or deactivation is not independently validated.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Sabotage or data destruction by a disgruntled departing employee
OrcaRisk.cause: Failure to proactively suspend active sessions, reset passwords, and sever network access the exact moment a hostile termination is executed.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
User Access Review
Access Deactivation Procedure 
Access Management Procedure
MBSS
Information Security Policy
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Existing access controls reduce the likelihood of unauthorized alteration or disruption of critical systems and data. However, stronger privileged-access restrictions, activity logging, change authorization, segregation of duties, backup protection, and monitoring of high-risk actions are required.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Critical data or systems may be altered, deleted, or disrupted, resulting in business interruption, financial loss, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because failure to immediately suspend sessions, reset credentials, and terminate network access during hostile departures may allow departing employees to alter or destroy critical systems and data.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Existing access controls reduce the risk to Unlikely and Moderate. However, a disgruntled employee may still cause disruption where privileged access, active sessions, service accounts, backups, or high-risk activities are not immediately controlled and monitored.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Introduction of Segregation of Duties (SoD) conflicts
OrcaRisk.cause: Absence of automated SoD checks or manual risk assessments within the access request workflow before approval is granted.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
User Access Review
Access Deactivation Procedure 
Access Management Procedure
MBSS
Information Security Policy
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Access reviews and access management procedures provide partial control over incompatible access rights. However, a formal segregation-of-duties matrix, automated conflict detection, documented exceptions, compensating controls, and periodic conflict reassessment should be established or strengthened.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Conflicting access rights may enable fraud, unauthorized transactions, control failure, and audit findings.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because the absence of preventive segregation-of-duties checks may regularly allow conflicting permissions to be approved, potentially enabling fraud, unauthorized transactions, and significant control failures.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Access reviews and access-management procedures reduce the risk to Unlikely and Moderate. Residual risk remains because conflicts may not be identified before provisioning without a formal SoD matrix, automated checks, exception approvals, and compensating controls.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Granting excessive access to new hires beyond what is required for their role
OrcaRisk.cause: Lack of execution of RBAC and least privilege
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
User Access Review
Access Management Procedure
MBSS
Information Security Policy
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Access management procedures, baseline security requirements, and periodic reviews provide a foundation for appropriate access provisioning. However, role-based access profiles, documented approvals, least-privilege validation, onboarding checks, and post-provisioning verification require improvement.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: New employees may access systems or data beyond their role, increasing the risk of misuse, data exposure, and policy violations.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Major because inadequate implementation of role-based access and least privilege may regularly result in new employees receiving access beyond their job requirements, increasing the possibility of misuse or data exposure.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Access-management procedures and reviews reduce the risk to Rare and Minor. Residual exposure remains where role profiles are outdated, approvals are insufficiently validated, or post-provisioning checks are not consistently completed.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Successful phishing, spear-phishing, or Business Email Compromise attacks may result in credential compromise, unauthorized access, fraudulent transactions, malware delivery, data exposure, financial loss, regulatory findings, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.cause:
Low security awareness or poor phishing recognition - Employees may fail to identify suspicious links, attachments, impersonation attempts, fake login pages, or unusual payment/change requests.

Limited monitoring of suspicious mailbox activity - Unusual forwarding rules, login locations, impossible travel, mailbox delegation, inbox rule creation, and OAuth consent abuse may not be detected quickly.

Lack of phishing simulations and targeted training - Employees may not be regularly tested or coached on current phishing, spear-phishing, and BEC techniques.

Lack of strong email security controls - Insufficient protection against spoofing, malicious attachments, suspicious links, lookalike domains, and impersonation emails.

Weak or missing MFA - Compromised credentials can be used more easily when accounts do not require strong MFA, phishing-resistant MFA, or step-up authentication.

Poor password practices - Password reuse, weak passwords, shared credentials, or exposed credentials increase the likelihood of account takeover.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
Endpoint Security Policy
Email Security thru TrendMicro with CTP. 
Spreading cybersecurity awareness through slack channel and posters inside the office
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Endpoint security policies, Trend Micro email security, and awareness activities provide preventive controls against phishing and credential compromise. However, the overall email and endpoint security posture requires improvement in technical coverage, configuration, monitoring, phishing-resistant authentication, response procedures, and effectiveness testing.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Credential compromise and fraudulent activity may occur, resulting in unauthorized access, financial loss, data exposure, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because weaknesses in employee awareness, email monitoring, phishing simulations, authentication, password practices, and email-security controls may regularly enable phishing or BEC attacks with severe financial, operational, regulatory, and reputational consequences.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Trend Micro email security, endpoint requirements, and awareness activities reduce the risk to Possible and Major. However, sophisticated phishing, impersonation, credential theft, human error, and gaps in mailbox monitoring may still result in significant compromise or fraud.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Malware or ransomware execution on user devices may enable lateral movement across the environment, leading to credential compromise, unauthorized access to critical systems, data encryption or exfiltration, business disruption, financial loss, regulatory findings, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.cause:
Weak endpoint protection - Devices may lack properly configured EDR, antivirus, ransomware protection, behavior monitoring, or automated isolation capability.

Unpatched operating systems and applications - Known vulnerabilities in browsers, office tools, VPN clients, endpoint agents, or operating systems may be exploited to execute malware.

Excessive user privileges - Users with local admin rights or overprivileged access can allow malware to install tools, disable controls, access sensitive files, or move laterally.

Poor network segmentation - Flat networks allow malware to spread more easily from one compromised device to servers, databases, shared drives, or critical applications.

Inadequate device hardening - Missing restrictions on macros, scripts, PowerShell, USB usage, unsigned applications, and unauthorized software can increase malware execution risk.

Delayed containment - Slow isolation of infected endpoints, credential rotation, or blocking of indicators may allow the malware to spread.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
EDR - Provides endpoint-level threat detection, behavioral anomaly monitoring, malware detection, suspicious process/activity detection, and alerting for potential compromise. Supports investigation and response through endpoint telemetry, threat containment, and visibility into malicious activity on user devices.

UEM - Enforces device security and compliance controls, including device access management, patch management, configuration hardening, device inventory, policy enforcement, and remote lock/wipe capabilities to reduce the likelihood and impact of malware execution.
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: EDR and UEM provide significant endpoint visibility, threat detection, configuration enforcement, patching, inventory, and remote-response capabilities. However, improvements are required in device coverage, policy enforcement, alert tuning, response integration, patch compliance, exception handling, and periodic effectiveness validation.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Systems and data may be compromised or encrypted, causing business disruption, financial loss, regulatory findings, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Possible and Critical because weak endpoint protection, unpatched devices, excessive privileges, poor segmentation, inadequate hardening, or delayed containment may allow malware or ransomware to spread and significantly disrupt critical operations.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: EDR and UEM reduce the potential impact to Minor, but the likelihood remains Possible because malware may still execute where device coverage, patching, configuration enforcement, alert tuning, or containment processes are incomplete.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive corporate data from endpoints may result in data leakage, regulatory violations, financial loss, legal exposure, loss of customer trust, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.cause:
Weak endpoint data loss prevention controls - Endpoints may not have DLP controls to detect, block, or alert on sensitive data transfers.

Uncontrolled use of removable media - Users may copy sensitive files to USB drives, external hard drives, or other removable storage without restriction.

Use of unauthorized cloud storage or file-sharing tools - Sensitive corporate data may be uploaded to personal Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, email, messaging apps, or other unsanctioned platforms.

Compromised user devices - Malware, RATs, infostealers, or threat actors may exfiltrate files directly from infected endpoints.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
From a CyberSecurity governance perspective: Data exfiltration policy in Google Workspace, Information Security Policy, Data Classification Policy, Endpoint Security Policy are in place.

From a protective/detective technology perspective:
Amazon Guard Duty - Helps detect potential exfiltration involving AWS workloads or cloud resources, but does not directly prevent data movement from user endpoints.

Google Workspace Built-in DLP - Helps reduce leakage through approved Google Workspace channels, but may not fully cover endpoint-level actions such as USB transfer, local file copying, personal cloud apps, messaging apps, or malware-based exfiltration.

UEM - Enforces endpoint security policies such as device compliance, encryption, remote lock/wipe, application restrictions, configuration baselines, and device access controls.
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Governance controls, Google Workspace DLP, AWS GuardDuty, and UEM collectively provide documented preventive and detective measures against data exfiltration. The controls are considered effective based on the stated implementation, although continued monitoring and periodic coverage reviews should be maintained, particularly for endpoint and non-approved communication channels.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Sensitive corporate or customer data may be leaked, resulting in privacy violations, financial loss, legal exposure, and loss of trust.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because weak endpoint DLP, unrestricted removable media, unauthorized cloud services, and compromised devices may regularly permit sensitive information to be exfiltrated, resulting in serious privacy, legal, financial, and reputational consequences.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Governance policies, Google Workspace DLP, GuardDuty, and UEM reduce the risk to Possible and Moderate. Residual exposure remains for USB transfers, local copying, personal cloud services, messaging applications, and malware-based endpoint exfiltration not fully covered by existing controls.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Delivery of malicious payloads (malware/ransomware) via email attachments or links
OrcaRisk.cause: Ineffective email filtering and lack of sandboxing for unknown attachments.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
Awareness training for all employees on clicking malicious links.
Email quarantine of of the emails containing malicious contents.
Email security through TrendMicro
Information Security Policy
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Security awareness, email quarantine, Trend Micro email protection, and the Information Security Policy provide multiple layers of protection against malicious emails. However, control effectiveness should be improved through phishing simulations, configuration reviews, advanced impersonation protection, reporting metrics, incident trend analysis, and timely remediation of identified weaknesses.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Malware infection or ransomware may occur, resulting in system compromise, data loss, operational disruption, and financial impact.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because ineffective email filtering and limited sandboxing may repeatedly allow malicious attachments or links to reach employees, potentially resulting in malware infection, ransomware, data loss, and major operational disruption.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Awareness training, email quarantine, Trend Micro protection, and security policies reduce the risk to Unlikely and Moderate. However, new or obfuscated payloads, configuration weaknesses, and employee interaction with malicious content may still result in compromise.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Inability to retrieve critical communications
OrcaRisk.cause: False quarantined by the email security tool
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: Configure email security tools
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Email security tools are configured and operating as a preventive and detective control against malicious email content. The control is considered effective, subject to continued rule tuning, signature updates, configuration reviews, alert monitoring, and periodic testing against emerging email threats.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Important business, audit, regulatory, or investigation records may be unavailable, affecting decision-making, compliance, and incident response.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Major because legitimate communications may repeatedly be falsely quarantined, making important business, regulatory, audit, or investigation records unavailable when needed.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Proper email-security configuration reduces the risk to Unlikely and Minor. Limited residual exposure remains from rule-tuning errors, false positives, delayed quarantine review, or failure to restore legitimate communications promptly.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Introduction of vulnerabilities via unapproved or pirated software (Shadow IT)
OrcaRisk.cause: Lack of application whitelisting controls.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: Whitelisting of applications through Unified Endpoint Management Tool (Jumpcloud)
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Application whitelisting through JumpCloud UEM effectively restricts the installation or execution of unauthorized applications. Continued effectiveness depends on complete device enrollment, controlled exception approvals, periodic whitelist reviews, monitoring of bypass attempts, and timely policy updates.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Vulnerable or unauthorized software may introduce malware, licensing issues, data exposure, and compliance violations.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because the absence of application whitelisting may regularly allow unauthorized, vulnerable, or pirated software to be installed, potentially introducing malware, licensing violations, data exposure, and significant compliance issues.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: JumpCloud application whitelisting reduces the risk to Unlikely and Minor. Residual exposure remains where devices are not enrolled, exceptions are poorly controlled, policies are outdated, or users bypass restrictions.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Unauthorized access to corporate email accounts via credential stuffing or brute-force attacks
OrcaRisk.cause: Weak password policies.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
Enforcing strong password policies 
Access Management Procedure
Google Authentication
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Strong password requirements, the Access Management Procedure, and Google authentication provide an effective authentication framework. Effectiveness should be maintained through periodic configuration reviews, MFA enforcement where applicable, monitoring of suspicious authentication activity, and timely revocation of compromised credentials.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Corporate email accounts may be compromised, resulting in data exposure, impersonation, fraud, and phishing attacks.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because weak password practices may repeatedly expose corporate email accounts to credential stuffing and brute-force attacks, potentially enabling impersonation, fraud, phishing, and data exposure.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Strong password requirements, Google authentication, and access-management procedures reduce the risk to Unlikely and Incidental. Residual exposure remains from stolen credentials, session hijacking, authentication misconfiguration, or accounts not fully covered by MFA.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Shadow IT - Risk of assets that could not be tracked
OrcaRisk.cause: Inconsistent adherence to the hardening process for laptop asset management
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
1. Implementation of MBSS policy
2. Asset Management Policy
3. End point security policy
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: The MBSS, Asset Management Policy, and Endpoint Security Policy establish governance requirements for managing and securing information assets. However, improvements are required in implementation consistency, asset discovery, ownership assignment, compliance monitoring, patching, and enforcement across all applicable assets.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Unknown assets may remain unmanaged, unpatched, or unmonitored, increasing the risk of data exposure, compromise, and compliance gaps.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Frequent and Critical because inconsistent adherence to laptop hardening and asset-management processes may regularly leave unknown assets untracked, unpatched, or unmonitored, potentially resulting in compromise, data exposure, and serious compliance gaps.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: The MBSS, Asset Management Policy, and Endpoint Security Policy reduce the risk to Unlikely and Moderate. However, assets may still remain unidentified or non-compliant where discovery, ownership, inventory reconciliation, hardening, and enforcement are inconsistent.
OrcaRisk.actionItems: Creation of a Physical Asset Security Policy

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Stolen, Missing and Damaged Devices
OrcaRisk.cause:
Lack of physical storage security
Employee Negligence
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
UEM
Asset Tagging
Asset Inventory
Physical Asset Incident Report Form
Physical Asset Management Policy
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: UEM, asset tagging, asset inventory, incident reporting, and the Physical Asset Management Policy provide a structured asset-management framework. However, reconciliation, inventory accuracy, assignment accountability, lifecycle tracking, periodic verification, and timely investigation of missing or unaccounted assets require improvement.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Corporate data may be lost or exposed, resulting in privacy breaches, operational disruption, financial loss, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is rated Likely and Moderate because insufficient physical-storage security may result in devices being stolen, misplaced, or damaged, potentially causing data exposure, operational delays, financial loss, and reputational damage.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: UEM, asset tagging, inventory, incident reporting, and physical-asset procedures reduce the risk to Unlikely and Minor. Residual exposure remains from inventory inaccuracies, delayed loss reporting, inadequate storage, or devices not properly enrolled and encrypted.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Lack of inventory of available due to budget constraints resulting in no devices provided to new employees.
OrcaRisk.cause: Budget
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls:
1. Laptop re-assignment
2. Hardware inventory
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: Laptop reassignment and hardware inventory provide visibility over available devices and help maximize the use of existing assets. However, the controls do not fully address insufficient device availability caused by budget constraints. Improvements are required in inventory accuracy, device forecasting, minimum buffer-stock requirements, timely recovery and reassignment, budget planning, and proper sanitization and hardening of reassigned laptops.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Assets may be untracked, unmanaged, or improperly assigned, resulting in control gaps, loss of accountability, and audit findings.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is considered significant because budget limitations may frequently result in an insufficient number of available corporate devices for new employees. This may delay employee onboarding and productivity or lead to the use of personal, shared, or unauthorized devices, increasing the risk of inadequate security configuration, data exposure, asset-accountability gaps, and non-compliance with endpoint security requirements.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Laptop reassignment and hardware inventory controls help maximize the use of available devices and provide visibility over device availability, ownership, condition, and allocation. However, residual risk remains where the number of serviceable devices is insufficient, inventory records are inaccurate, device recovery or reassignment is delayed, or reassigned devices are not properly sanitized, hardened, and configured before being issued to new employees.

OrcaRisk.riskThreat: Outdated Policies, Standards, Procedures, and Guidelines.
OrcaRisk.cause: No annual review and updates within the cybersecurity team.
OrcaRisk.existingKeyControls: 1. Annual review and update of policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines.
OrcaRisk.overallControlEffectivenessRemarks: The annual review and update requirement establishes a formal mechanism for maintaining current governance documents. However, the control requires stronger implementation through assigned document owners, a centralized review calendar, monitoring of overdue reviews, documented regulatory and business-change assessments, timely approval, version control, and communication of updated requirements to relevant stakeholders.
OrcaRisk.impactPerRisk: Security practices may become misaligned with regulatory and business requirements, resulting in control gaps, audit findings, and non-compliance.
OrcaRisk.inherentRiskRatingRemarks: The risk is considered significant because the absence of regular reviews may cause information security policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines to become outdated or misaligned with changes in regulatory requirements, business operations, technologies, threats, and organizational responsibilities. This may result in control gaps, inconsistent practices, audit findings, and regulatory non-compliance.
OrcaRisk.residualRiskRemarks: Annual review and update of policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines reduces the likelihood that governance documents will become outdated or misaligned. However, residual risk remains where reviews are delayed, regulatory or business changes occur between annual review cycles, document owners fail to incorporate relevant requirements, or revised documents are not promptly approved, communicated, and implemented.
